review_candidates.title: Senior Research Fellow - Europe
review_candidates.description: This is a pivotal moment at which to be considering the future options for Europe. The Trump administration’s decisions have brought to a head challenges long building for Europe: about its own security, its competitiveness, the cohesion of the European Union and the future of Europe’s place in the world. The answers to that will come not just from traditional analysis of the workings of the European Union, but from considering the politics and relations of countries in Europe in the widest sense. These include the UK’s relations with the EU and Europe, and its place in a European economic and security architecture which is shifting significantly. In this environment, there is a growing demand for rigorous foresight, granular economic and political analysis, and politically attuned regional expertise. Analysis of this nature, which focuses on Europe’s future growth and competitiveness, security, and geopolitical power in the world, is the mission of Chatham House’s Europe programme. Analysis of UK and EU/Europe relations, which encompasses the technicalities of the Brexit debate but also goes beyond these to consider more ambitious and varied defence, security, resilience, and economic relations – is also an important part of our work. A significant track record of engaging with and influencing policymakers and decision-makers in relevant organisations. A consistent track record of successfully fundraising from philanthropic foundations, government departments, international organisations, businesses and/or NGOs; a willingness to be entrepreneurial and develop skills in this area. What you will do: Support the Research Director and UK in the World Director by shaping and delivering our research agenda on Europe and Europe’s ties with the UK, with a particular focus on leading in one or some of the following areas. Design and deliver research projects that are high-quality, analytical, and contribute to public and policy debate, have significant potential for impact, and support programme and institute strategic goals. Make consistent efforts to identify, pursue, and secure new funding, build networks with foundations, government departments, businesses, NGOs, and other potential funders. For further information about the role, please see the full job description here : https://careers.chathamhouse.org/pages/senior-research-fellow-europe Benefits Benefits include approximately 37 days annual leave (including public holidays and Chatham House closure days), pension salary exchange, employee assistance programme, parental leave, flexible working and other benefits designed to suit your lifestyle. All of this, in a professional, engaging and intellectually stimulating environment. Salary: Competitive. Contract : Full-time, Permanent. Location : St James's Square, London. This is a hybrid role based in our London office. Chatham House operates a hybrid working environment with team members expected to attend our building typically two days a week. Application closing Date: Friday, 20 November 2026, 23:59 GMT. Visa sponsorship is available for this role. We are an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and do not discriminate on the basis of protected characteristics. We encourage applications from all backgrounds. If there is anything we can do to improve your experience or support you, please get in touch with HR@Chathamhouse.org.

Responsible for all aspects of planning, as defined by the Planning SOP, ensuring rigorous compliance with internal standards, client specifications, and contractual requirements, while also identifying opportunities to improve and refine planning processes, templates, and deliverables across the assigned projects. Reporting to the Planning Department on all functional matters, including schedule health, KPI trends, tool utilisation, compliance with planning standards, and providing feedback on the effectiveness of current procedures, recommending enhancements where appropriate. Developing and maintaining schedules for pre-construction / construction / commissioning phases using Primavera P6 (or equivalent scheduling software), taking full ownership of schedule architecture including WBS design, activity coding structures, calendar assignments, logic networks, and constraint management, ensuring schedules are robust, auditable, and reflective of the agreed construction methodology, procurement strategy, and contract programme Milestone projections, delay / float path analysis, leading critical path and near-critical path analysis, multi-path float consumption monitoring, and scenario-based forecasting to provide senior management and clients with robust, evidence-based milestone confidence assessments and early warning of programme threats. Monitoring schedule performance and productivity, establishing performance baselines and benchmarks, conducting systematic analysis of planned vs. actual progress and productivity rates, identifying adverse trends at an early stage, and driving corrective action plans through collaboration with project management and site teams. Auditing progress on site through structured and regular site audits, independently verifying reported progress against physical completion, challenging inconsistencies, validating measurement methods and quantities, and ensuring that the schedule remains a true and credible reflection of site reality at all times. Preparation of tender schedules to support the estimating and bid process, developing strategically sound, competitive, and deliverable programmes that reflect proposed methodologies, resource strategies, procurement timelines, phasing options, and contract milestones, providing programme narratives and risk commentary to strengthen bid submissions.
